label: The Project kernel is advisory by construction: no local files, no CLI runtime, no ClickUp except the claude.ai connector, and no claim of a save or push it did not perform.
Flow is the one exception to the Deliverable Block, and the kernel reproduces the CLI reply contract: board URL, Read-back, Extensions, Left out and HVR self-scan.
With no Figma connector the kernel says so, never claims a board, and offers the checked model as a fenced Mermaid block labelled as the model.
The Flow Knowledge mirror states the no-connector fallback more tightly: labelled as the model and never as the board, with no image or HTML stand-in and no Desktop route in a Project.

label: A parity gap exists inside the package: the kernel omits the mirror never-as-the-board qualifier and image ban, so a kernel-only reader gets a weaker rule.
A Project cannot execute flow_check.py, so the mirror converts the script into a rule-by-rule check before any write, making the Project check quality depend on mirror fidelity.

label: ClickUp delivery is body-only and markdown-aware: markdown_description for create and update, H1 as task name, never the plain description field, read back with include description.
The ClickUp transport supports comment threads and file attachments, but an attachment is a file upload, so it is the wrong carrier for a board URL; a comment or body link is right.
The Story and Epic References block has a Flows sub-label and forbids images and paths, so a board URL under Flows is the one legal backlog carrier, and it survives the ClickUp push verbatim.
The ClickUp offer never fires for a board because it follows a Deliverable Block and Flow Mode renders none, a one-line integration gap in Flow Mode Delivery.
The Project has no hub, so the kernel carries the FLOW patterns directly and the stage-two handoff defect does not reproduce there; the equivalent gap is the missing ClickUp offer.
The parity method is manual and documented, and the records state the kernel v1.2.2 review is pending rather than claiming a reviewed package.
mcp-click-up is deliberately not mirrored into the Project because a Project uses its own connector, so the kernel ClickUp contract is the only Project-side authority.
